purpose: The confirmation behind a press-and-hold on a card or hero. It names the title, lists only the actions that card supports, and acts on a deliberate second OK.

anatomy.note: 0xA6 black, clickable, focusable=false; click closes unchanged.
560dp wide, pack surface, 1dp line, radius.panel, 22/18/22/16 padding. The Glass pack wears a liquid-glass lens here (radius.panel) instead of the painted plate.
'Choose what to do with this title', type.panelNote ink3.

One row per action: type.panelRow bold, 16/14 padding, 8dp gap, first row 18dp after the note. Sizes come from the pack's type scale, never raw SP, so a large system font scale cannot grow the rows out of the panel.
'Back closes without changing anything', type.panelNote ink3, 12dp below the last row.

geometry.focus: rows show a 0x2E white plate on focus

copy.note: Choose what to do with this title

rules: Rows own LEFT/RIGHT (self-linked); UP/DOWN step and stop at the ends.
The sheet is a trap: focus cannot leave it while open.
Back closes without running any action and returns focus to the card it came from.
A second open is refused while one sheet is up.

behaviour: Choosing a row closes the sheet first, then runs the action.
The action list is derived from the card's current state, never hard-coded to two entries.
The sheet is pack furniture (surface, radius, ink), not a system dialog.
A card opens it on a hold, on a press the input stack itself marks long-press or repeats while down, and on the MENU (⋮) key.
Only a sheet still attached to a window counts as open, so a screen destroyed under one cannot silence later holds.

Hiding a row writes the hub's rows record (GET then POST /app/v1/prefs), the same record Settings › Home rows edits; the page drops that shelf in place and moves focus to the shelf that took its place.

platformDeltas.ios: Present as a context menu/action sheet with the same actions and copy; long-press opens it.
platformDeltas.windows: Right-click opens the same list; Escape closes unchanged.
platformDeltas.apple-tv: Same sheet; focus lift on rows.
